principles.text: When he starts feeling bearish he's usually too early; don't predict, just react — keep buying longs while the market shows strength until it actually shows weakness or stops you out.
Don't chase: wait for a tight 5-minute pullback to enter rather than buying the extension up high, which would have gotten the '2022 me' stopped out.
Only put actionable names (the ones you'd actually enter) in your main watch list; keep the real extended leaders in a separate 'leading names' list to keep the main list focused.

Size up slowly, not immediately. After the early-2025 lesson, when the account grows from e.g. 10K to 20K he keeps risking near the original 1% dollar amount (e.g. ~150 instead of 200), only stepping up gradually (110 at 13K, 120 at 15K).
The best buys come at the very beginning of a move; entries get progressively lower-quality afterward, so sizing up immediately right when pullback odds rise leads to more stop-outs.
Sizing up slowly on the way up is a precaution that makes it easier to size down on the way down; his biggest past mistake was raising risk on the way up and failing to size down on the way down.
While the market keeps grinding higher, it's good to sell some into strength and not get so excited you forget the downside risk.
For names that like to gap above the 9/21 EMA after a pullback and turn higher, you must get in fast when it turns up; a tight risk is available on the gap-up day.
